full_text_en:
Li Erjiao v. Zhang Shihui — Dispute over Agency by Mandate

Plaintiff: Li Erjiao, female, 66 years old, residing at Xili Baimang Village, Nanshan District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Zhang Shihui, male, 26 years old, business clerk of the Foreign Economic Company of Nanshan District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Third Party: Zhang Shiqin, female, 23 years old, residing at No. 4 Nanji Road, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

The plaintiff, Li Erjiao, filed an action with the Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, regarding a dispute over agency by mandate with the defendant, Zhang Shihui. After examining the case, the Nanshan District People's Court found that the outcome of the case had a legal interest with Zhang Shiqin, and pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, notified her to participate in the proceedings.

The Nanshan District People's Court found upon trial: The plaintiff Li Erjiao's husband, Zhang Yaluo, subscribed for shares (1 yuan per share) in the Nantou Credit Cooperative of Shenzhen in the 1950s. When the Shenzhen Development Bank was established in 1987, the said two shares were converted into 180 shares. During the distribution of dividends and share increase in 1990, the 180 shares were further increased to 288 shares. Zhang Yaluo, the original subscriber, died in 1988, and the stock certificates for the 288 shares were held by the plaintiff. Previously, Zhang Yaluo had entrusted the defendant Zhang Shihui to collect dividends from the securities company and to handle procedures such as share increases. In April 1990, the plaintiff gave the stock certificates to the defendant, entrusting him to collect dividends on her behalf. On April 25, 1990, the defendant, through the securities company, transferred the 288 shares registered under Zhang Yaluo's name to the name of his sister, the third party Zhang Shiqin, at a price of 3.56 yuan per share. After deducting taxes and handling fees, the defendant entrusted his mother, Wu Yuanyou, to deliver the dividends and the proceeds from the sale of the shares, totaling 890 yuan, to the plaintiff. On August 25 of the same year, after the plaintiff showed the receipt to her son-in-law, she discovered that the 288 shares of the Development Bank had been transferred by the defendant to the name of Zhang Shiqin. The plaintiff demanded the return of the stock certificates from the defendant, but the defendant refused, and she therefore filed the lawsuit with the court in April 1991.

The Nanshan District People's Court held: An agent shall carry out civil juristic acts in the name of the principal within the scope of the agency. If an agent exceeds the scope of the agency, the principal shall bear civil liability only if the act is ratified by the principal. For acts not ratified, the actor shall bear civil liability. The plaintiff Li Erjiao only entrusted the defendant Zhang Shihui to collect dividends on her behalf, but Zhang Shihui arbitrarily sold the plaintiff's shares at a low price and transferred them to the third party Zhang Shiqin. His conduct violated the provisions of Article 66 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, exceeded the scope of his agency, and he shall bear civil liability. During the trial, Li Erjiao voluntarily waived the bonus shares distributed on the disputed shares in 1991 and only demanded that Zhang Shihui purchase and return 288 shares of the Development Bank. Zhang Shihui expressed agreement, which should be permitted. Accordingly, on September 12, 1991, through mediation by the court, the plaintiff and the defendant reached the following agreement:

1. Before September 14, 1991, the defendant Zhang Shihui shall, using the plaintiff Li Erjiao's identity card and name, purchase 288 shares of Shenzhen Development Bank stock for Li Erjiao. The required share capital and handling fees shall be borne by Zhang Shihui.
2. The plaintiff Li Erjiao shall return in court the 890 yuan delivered by the defendant Zhang Shihui in April 1990.
